narrative: PL1__MAB0D63B exhibits stable demand (CV=0.19) averaging 52,959 units/day across 87 working days with no statistically significant trend. Lead times show moderate variability (CV=0.49, mean 2.46 days) driven primarily by transport uncertainty. The (r,Q) policy is selected because stable normal demand with a well-defined EOQ (660,995) far exceeding the MOQ (53,091) makes continuous-review fixed-quantity replenishment optimal. Establishing a safety stock of 107,814 units achieves the 95% service level while cutting total annual replenishment cost by 81.4% versus the current SAP MOQ-driven policy.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is stable and approximately normally distributed (CV=0.19); lead time variability is moderate but well-characterized. These conditions satisfy the classical (r,Q) model assumptions. The EOQ (660,995) is well above the MOQ (53,091), so MOQ is non-binding and the economic quantity governs, yielding a large consolidation benefit.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity constraint binds: safety_stock + order_quantity = 768,809 units vs. max_storage = 1,363,206 (56.4% utilisation). Headroom of 594,397 units provides ample buffer. No service or cost risk from capacity. Transport is the dominant lead-time variance contributor (50%); reducing transport variability would lower sigma_LTD and allow a ~10% reduction in safety stock.
